followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified retrieval/listing task with clear completion criteria (40 boys' names, 40 girls' names of semi-common Japanese names). There are a few reasons Lapwing fits well:

1. **Task type match**: This is fundamentally an extraction/recall task with a defined format and quantity, not open-ended creative invention. Lapwing's top-rated tasks are exactly this kind of well-specified retrieval and reformatting work.

2. **Capability**: The internal eval differences between the two models on the relevant categories (Extraction & Retrieval, and even Creative Generation) are within run-to-run variance, so neither model has a meaningful quality edge here.

3. **Preference alignment matters at the margin**: Since capability is effectively tied, I leaned on which model self-reports liking this kind of task. Dunlin's preferences trend strongly toward open-ended, novel, high-latitude invention — a structured "list 40 + 40" task sits at the low-latitude end it favors least. Lapwing, while it self-reports mild aversion to open-ended work, treats clearly-bounded list/retrieval tasks as its preferred family.

The user's "don't half-ass it" note signals they want a complete, correctly-counted, well-organized response — which favors the model oriented toward precise, criteria-driven completion. That's Lapwing.
